newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania court hears former PM in miners' boss trial.
newsitem.headline: Romania court hears former PM in miners' boss trial.

text.p: Former Romanian prime minister Petre Roman testified on Tuesday in the trial of a vigilante miners' leader accused of spearheading riots which toppled his government in 1991.
Miners' union boss Miron Cosma sat in the dock as Roman told the court about the violence which killed three people when Cosma's miners clashed with security forces and ransacked government offices.
"This trial meets the need to reinforce the rule of law in Romania," Roman told Reuters, emerging from the three-hour hearing before two judges.
Cosma, 43, is charged with undermining state authority and breaking firearms laws, offences which could carry a jail sentence of up to 15 years.
"I testified in order to do my duty as a citizen," said Roman, now chairman of parliament's upper house, the Senate.
"The government was ousted in a coup," Roman told the court. He blamed the 1991 riots on hardliners backing ex-president Ion Iliescu, a former communist.

Iliescu has publicly denied the accusations and denounced Cosma's arrest as "exaggerated". The former president is one of 360 witnesses due to give evidence at the trial, which is expected to last several months.
"The miners were manipulated," Cosma told the court on Tuesday. "Roman's place should be here, next to me in the dock," he shouted at the end of the hearing.
"Sentence me, jail me wherever you want, I cannot accept this kind of justice. It is a political trial," said Cosma, who was arrested earlier this year and has already been on trial for four months.
Roman's Democrats are junior partners in the centrist coalition government which took office after Iliescu and his leftists were defeated in November 1996 elections.

Reformist president Emil Constantinescu has pledged to bring to justice those responsible for successive waves of political violence in the early post-communist years, which culminated in the September 1991 anti-government rioting.
